environment.label: Environment
environment.description: Basic weather and environmental conditions at the sensor location.

airQuality.label: Air Quality
airQuality.description: Particulate matter — tiny particles suspended in the air that can affect health when inhaled.

uv.label: UV Radiation
uv.description: Ultraviolet radiation from the sun, measured in three wavelength bands.

particleCounts.label: Particle Counts
particleCounts.description: Number of particles per size category in a 0.1 liter air sample. Complements mass-based PM measurements.

health.label: Sensor Health
health.description: Operational status of the sensor hardware.

noiseDba.label: Noise
noiseDba.description: A-weighted sound pressure level — the standard measurement for environmental noise. Prolonged exposure above 70 dBA can cause hearing damage.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.description: Air temperature measured by the sensor. Affected by direct sunlight and nearby heat sources.

humidity.label: Humidity
humidity.description: Relative humidity — the amount of moisture in the air. Comfortable range is 30–60%.

lightLux.label: Light
lightLux.description: Ambient light intensity. Full daylight is ~10,000–25,000 lux. Office lighting is ~300–500 lux.

pressurePa.label: Pressure
pressurePa.description: Atmospheric pressure. Standard sea-level pressure is 101.325 kPa. Changes indicate weather shifts.

pm1.label: PM1
pm1.description: Ultra-fine particles smaller than 1 micrometer. Can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream.

pm25.label: PM2.5
pm25.description: Fine particles smaller than 2.5 micrometers — the most health-relevant air quality metric. Main sources: traffic, combustion, dust.

pm4.label: PM4
pm4.description: Particles smaller than 4 micrometers. Includes PM2.5 plus some coarser particles.

pm10.label: PM10
pm10.description: Coarse particles smaller than 10 micrometers. Sources include dust, pollen, and road wear. Can irritate the respiratory system.

uvA.label: UVA
uvA.description: Long-wave UV (315–400nm). Penetrates deep into skin, causes aging. Present year-round, passes through clouds and glass.

uvB.label: UVB
uvB.description: Medium-wave UV (280–315nm). Causes sunburn and is the primary risk factor for skin cancer. Strongest midday in summer.

uvC.label: UVC
uvC.description: Short-wave UV (100–280nm). Mostly absorbed by the atmosphere. Readings near zero are normal.

pn05.label: PN0.5
pn05.description: Count of particles larger than 0.5 µm. The smallest particles detected — high counts indicate combustion sources.

pn10.label: PN1.0
pn10.description: Count of particles larger than 1.0 µm.

pn25.label: PN2.5
pn25.description: Count of particles larger than 2.5 µm.

pn40.label: PN4.0
pn40.description: Count of particles larger than 4.0 µm.

pn100.label: PN10
pn100.description: Count of particles larger than 10 µm. These are coarse particles like dust and pollen.

tps.label: Typical Size
tps.description: The most common particle size in the sample. Helps identify the source — small (~0.5 µm) suggests combustion, large (~10 µm) suggests dust.

battery.label: Battery
battery.description: Remaining battery charge. Sensors at Skroutz stores are plugged in, so this should stay high.

rssi.label: WiFi RSSI
rssi.description: WiFi signal strength. Above -50 is excellent, -50 to -70 is good, below -70 may cause connectivity issues.

sdCard.label: SD Card
sdCard.description: Whether the SD card is present (1) or absent (0). Used for offline data buffering.

about.title: About Soundwatch Athens
about.intro: Athens consistently ranks among the noisiest capitals in Europe. Noise pollution is a critical urban challenge with direct impacts on public health and quality of life.
about.introProblem: Despite the scale of the problem, Athens today lacks a public, accessible noise monitoring network. Without data, the problem remains invisible and the conversation around solutions is based on assumptions.
about.mission: Soundwatch Athens aims to fill this gap — not just by measuring noise, but by empowering citizens with the data they need to advocate for a better quality of life in their neighborhood.
about.howItWorks: Each sensor measures noise levels (in dBA) locally on the device and transmits only the computed value — never raw audio — ensuring complete privacy. The data flows in real-time to this platform, where it's visualized on the interactive map.
about.openData: All sensor data is freely available through our public API. Anyone can access the data programmatically to build their own tools, conduct research, or advocate for change in their neighborhood.
about.whoWeAre: Soundwatch Athens is built by <schemaLabs>Schema Labs</schemaLabs> with the support of <skroutz>Skroutz</skroutz>, which hosts the sensor network at its physical stores across Athens. Community partner <astylab>Astylab</astylab> activates its ecosystem for urban transformation.
about.technology: Built on the open-source <link>Smart Citizen Kit</link> platform. All software developed for Soundwatch is <repo>open source</repo>.
